name: NSEFO-SIM
_notes: NSE Futures & Options runs on the same NNF Trimmed Protocol as Capital
Market, but is NOT the same dialect: transaction codes collide numerically
with CM's (2000 is BOARD_LOT_IN at both) but decode to different, larger
structures, and every private tag lives in this venue's own 9400+ range,
never CM's. See docs/specs/NSE_FO_TRANSCRIPTION.md and
exchangesim/venues/nsefo/transactions.py's module docstring for the full
list of collisions -- this is why nsefo/ has its own dictionary.py,
layouts.py and transactions.py rather than sharing Capital Market's.
Contract identity is the genuinely new part. Capital Market keys a
security on Symbol+Series; F&O keys a contract on CONTRACT_DESC --
instrument family, symbol, expiry, strike and option type. This
simulator renders one canonical name for every surface (the book, the
audit, the board, the control plane): 'NIFTY-FUTIDX-24SEP2026' for a
future, 'RELIANCE-OPTSTK-24SEP2026-2800-CE' for an option. 'resolve_symbol'
forgives case, '_'/space in place of '-', an ISO expiry, and a strike
with or without trailing zeroes, and accepts an unambiguous partial (a
symbol and instrument family, or a symbol/instrument family/expiry, that
together name exactly one contract) -- an ambiguous one is refused rather
than guessed. A wire order is matched to a contract by an exact lookup on
the five decoded CONTRACT_DESC fields, never through the forgiving path.
There are two listeners, exactly as Capital Market has. 'nnf.port' is
the gateway, where members trade. 'gateway_router.port' is the separate
port a member dials FIRST, to collect the session key, cryptographic
key, IV and additional key that encrypt the gateway connection. Both are
joined by the Box ID -- and Box IDs here (101-103) are chosen not to
collide with Capital Market's (1-3), since both venues may run at once
from the same repo clone.
'nnf.stream' is the machine/stream number this venue stamps on every
message (the header's TimeStamp2) and the one a DOWNLOAD_REQUEST must
name, 1 to 127. It is also the count SYSTEM_INFORMATION_OUT advertises
in AlphaChar, which is what a member loops its message download over; a
member asking for any other stream gets an empty download rather than an
error, since refusing would stop that loop. 'nnf.recovery_capacity' is
how many messages per user that download can still replay -- a ring, not
a trading day, so a soak test cannot run the process out of memory. The
cursor a member resumes from is the header's TimeStamp1, in jiffies.
'gateway_router.dynamic_iv' is how the dynamic half of the IV is laid
out under the 'new' methodology -- the one value here that is NOT
big-endian, since it is the memory of a C struct rather than a wire
field. 'auto' (the default) settles it on whichever of 'little' and
'big' authenticates a box's first message and logs the answer; set it
to either name to pin it and refuse the other. The exchange issues the
counter itself as zero, which is where the two readings coincide.
To reach this simulator from another machine, bind 'nnf.host' and
'gateway_router.host' to 0.0.0.0. The GR response's IPAddress is a
member's only statement of where the gateway is, so a gateway bound to
every interface answers with the address that member reached the router
on; 'gateway_router.advertise_host' (15 characters at most, the width
of the field) overrides that for a NAT or a port forward.
'gateway_router.tls' is set to '1.2' here, not the specification's own
'1.3' default: this project's Windows development interpreter (venv36,
OpenSSL 1.0.2q) cannot serve TLS 1.3 at all, and the venue refuses to
start rather than silently serving something weaker if asked for '1.3'
there. '1.2' is a floor, not a ceiling -- under OpenSSL 3.x it still
negotiates 1.3 when both ends support it. See
exchangesim/venues/nse/gateway_router.py's docstring for the full TLS
story, which is identical here; and rules.ASSUMPTIONS for why the
generated CA (var/tls-fo/gr_ca_cert1.pem -- a directory of its own, so
the two venues' generated certificates never collide) stands in for a
real exchange-issued one.
Only the Regular Lot book of the Normal market is traded, across FUTIDX,
FUTSTK, OPTIDX and OPTSTK. Special Terms, Stop Loss/MIT, Negotiated
Trade and every other book are rejected with their own published error
codes; so are All Or None, Minimum Fill, disclosed quantity, Good Till
Cancelled/Good Till Date, give-up (a populated CounterPartyBrokerId), the
self-trade-prevention STPC bit, and the whole Spread/2L/3L order family
(refused by transaction code, since no layout for its 480-byte structure
exists at all). See 'venue.assumptions' for the full list and every code.
The pre-open and Postclose market phases are published
(docs/specs/NSE_FO_TRANSCRIPTION.md §2.2) but not built in this slice --
this venue runs OPEN, CLOSED and HALTED only, and 'state.set' refuses the
other two rather than folding them onto the nearest phase this venue does
run.
There is no self-trade prevention: this venue's core mode keys on the
participant code, which means something else here, exactly as Capital
Market has none. A market configured with any stp_mode but NONE is
refused at start-up.
Reference data defaults to exchangesim/venues/nsefo/reference/contracts.csv
-- an UNVERIFIED sample universe (see that file's own header): the
underlyings and instrument families are real, but the strikes, base
prices, ticks and circuit-filter percentages are plausible rather than
quoted. Override with:
"reference": {
"contracts": "reference/contracts.csv"
Each contract carries its own lot size, base price, tick and circuit
filter (a percentage of the base price), since F&O has no published
price ladder the way Capital Market's tick_sizes.csv transcribes one.
